decisions.reason: The coded-referral commission change does not alter the distinct no-referral commission amount; the accepted $12 no-referral amount is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
Changing the coded-referral commission to $35 does not change ticket issuance, and the separately accepted four-ticket rule is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
The landing-page requirements still advertise a $10 coded-referral commission and must reflect the newly accepted $35 amount.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The logic itself sounds good to me.

After 34 mints, the leaderboard now shows 24 tickets and 19 commissions, which is perfect.

The NFT attributes are still not right, though. My screenshots show that NFT #42 has 18 tickets and 9 x $35 commissions on the leaderboard, which is correct. When I open NFT #42, the top of the page also correctly displays 18 tickets and 14 referrals. However, its attributes still report only 6 referrals and $85 in total earnings.

decisions.reason: The commission amount does not change the requirement that NFT metadata accurately expose its underlying referral, ticket, and earnings data; the same message's observed metadata failure is already separately represented.
The coded-referral commission amount does not entail any change to Small Block winners, prize values, draw triggers, eligibility, or pool funding.

The accepted +$35 coded-referral commission appears inconsistent with the existing $30 mint price and $12 founder plus $8 prize-pool allocation, so it is unclear whether $35 is a new per-mint split amount or an accounting-balance behavior.
